title: The Big Haul
checkpoint: Phase 5 (School readiness) — new sound 'au' (the /or/ sound as in haul, taut and vault)
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book for the new sound 'au' — another way to write the /or/ sound your child knows from 'fork', used in haul, taut and vault. This spelling most often sits in the middle of a word.

pages.text: Nell had a big net to haul.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee gripping a rope attached to a large net at the pond edge, leaning back with all her weight. Comic scale — she is tiny, the net is not.

pages.text: The net was stuck. It was taut.
pages.illustration: The rope stretched bar-straight and quivering, the net snagged on something under the water. Draw the tension in the rope itself.
Moss arriving and taking hold of the rope behind Nell, both leaning back in a line. Teamwork composition.
Both of them straining, feet dug in, faces screwed up with effort, the rope creeping in inch by inch. Sweat and determination.

pages.text: It was a big, big haul!
pages.illustration: The net finally out on the bank, bulging with weed, an old boot and a great many small treasures. Detailed and rewarding to pore over.

pages.text: Nell did a vault for joy.
pages.illustration: Nell doing a somersault in mid-air out of sheer delight, drawn as a looping motion arc with a yellow blur at the end.
Moss attempting the same somersault and getting it entirely wrong — mid-tumble, legs everywhere, spikes bristling. Hilarious.

pages.text: It was the best haul yet.
pages.illustration: Closing page: the pair sitting on the upturned boot beside their haul at sunset, exhausted and triumphant. Warm gold across the pond.
